name: Grape Hyacinth
family: Asparagaceae, the asparagus family (the hyacinth group)
grown_as: The common garden grape hyacinth, deep blue. ⚠️ CHECK: William's is 'Ocean Magic', listed as Muscari aucheri: its spikes are mid blue below and white at the top, and M. aucheri has fewer, broader, often grey-green leaves. Drawn here as the common M. armeniacum.
habit: Tufts of floppy narrow leaves with upright flower stems 10 to 20 cm tall. Spreads quickly into mats by offsets and seed.

leaf.arrangement: Three to six leaves from the base of each bulb, arching and lying on the soil
leaf.outline: 15 to 30 cm long by 3 to 6 mm wide, even width; often longer than the flower stems
leaf.surface: Fleshy and soft, deeply channelled (grooved) along the upper side
leaf.colour: Mid green, often yellowing at the tips by flowering time

flower.form: A dense cone-shaped spike of tiny round bells, like a bunch of grapes upside down
flower.petals: Six tepals joined into a small urn-shaped bell, swollen in the middle and pinched at the mouth, with six tiny white teeth turned back round the rim
flower.colour: Deep cobalt blue; the top few flowers paler
flower.centre: Not seen: the mouth is a tiny white-rimmed hole
flower.carried: Twenty to forty bells packed tightly in an egg- or cone-shaped spike 2 to 4 cm long at the top of a bare stem, pointing down and outward

fruit: Inflated, papery capsules with three rounded flat wings, about 1 cm, green ripening to straw, along the stem; black seeds.
seedling: Not drawn. A single fine grass-like leaf.
winter: Leaves come up in autumn and sprawl on the soil through winter, a clear sign of the plant.

leaf: a narrow fleshy leaf grooved down the upper side
bloom: many tiny round bells packed in a cone-shaped spike
each bell pinched at the mouth with a white rim of tiny teeth
deep blue, paler at the top
bulb: a small round bulb 1.5 to 2 cm with pale brown papery skin
often with several small offset bulbs round it
shoots: narrow grooved leaves already up in autumn, lying over the soil
no flower spike yet: leaves only, which stay through winter
flower: dense blue spikes on short bare stems
floppy narrow leaves round the base, often as long as the stems
seedhead: papery three-winged pods along the stem
dormant: nothing above the soil in summer

look_alikes: Bluebell has larger bells hanging down one side of the stem. Muscari latifolium has one broad leaf and a two-tone spike. Spanish bluebell leaves are much broader. Young leaves look like grass or chives but are fleshy and grooved, and chives smell of onion.
